atoms.1: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) is treated with a combination of antibiotics.
atoms.2: The antibiotics used for treating PID cover the most likely pathogens.
atoms.3: The most likely pathogens for PID include Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
atoms.4: The most likely pathogens for PID include Chlamydia trachomatis.
atoms.5: The most likely pathogens for PID include anaerobes.
atoms.6: The most likely pathogens for PID include Gram-negative facultative bacteria.
atoms.7: The most likely pathogens for PID include streptococci.
atoms.8: The treatment regimen for PID typically includes a combination of a cephalosporin and doxycycline.
atoms.9: The treatment regimen for PID may include metronidazole.
atoms.10: For outpatient treatment of PID, a common regimen is ceftriaxone 250 mg intramuscularly in a single dose.
atoms.11: For outpatient treatment of PID, a common regimen includes doxycycline 100 mg orally twice a day for 14 days.
atoms.12: For outpatient treatment of PID, metronidazole 500 mg orally twice a day for 14 days may be included.
atoms.13: For inpatient treatment of PID, one option is cefotetan 2 g intravenously every 12 hours.
atoms.14: For inpatient treatment of PID, one option is cefoxitin 2 g intravenously every 6 hours.
atoms.15: For inpatient treatment of PID, doxycycline 100 mg orally or intravenously every 12 hours is included.
atoms.16: Patients with PID should be re-evaluated within 48-72 hours to ensure clinical improvement.
atoms.17: Sexual partners of patients with PID should also be treated to prevent reinfection.
